tei:titleStmt.tei:title: יוֹם זֶה לְכׇל דוֹרוֹת
Yom Zeh l'Khol Dorot, a piyyuṭ for Pesaḥ Sheni by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:div.tei:head: Yom Zeh l'Khol Dorot, a piyyuṭ for Pesaḥ Sheni by Isaac Gantwerk Mayer

tei:lg.tei:l: This day for all generations, in the month of shining light
Designated for a second festival so it can be remembered.

tei:div.tei:p: The righteous of the people were impure for the sake of the intelligent one
(As all his bones floated up, since with them he swore to be buried)
They were purified after midnight, but they still have a desire –
Righteous in their eyes to observe the festival of God!
The Merciful, in great lovingkindness, set for them a time
A small festival, for all who were impure, to be designated
Returning, if far away, every man will testify as a witness
A law forever and ever, from being cut off God will exempt!
It draws near – that day, in the land of Your holiness,
Your offering we will offer, in Your presence!
Who called to the man that said, “Stand, and let me listen” –
“Speak to the children of Israel and say...”

tei:note.tei:p: Ziv – Biblical name for the month of Iyyar. See I Kings 6:1
Namely, Joseph. Sukkah 25b records a tradition that the men in the Numbers 9 passage were carrying his coffin.

A tradition in the Mekhilta d’Rabbi Yishmael 13:19 and Sotah 13a records that Joseph’s coffin was made of metal, and sunk in the Nile, but when Moses reminded him that the time to fulfill the oath of Genesis 50:25 had arrived, the coffin floated up to the top of the river.
By which point one is no longer allowed to consume the Pesaḥ sacrifice
Moses, in the original source for Pesaḥ Sheni – Numbers 9:8
